Clean observation/judgement split: loader.py is the only filesystem module, analyzer.py is a pure Policy->Report transform with no I/O, clock or RNG, and the resolution context (home, cwd) is a DECLARED Environment rather than a discovered one, so a committed fixture and a live settings stack grade through identical code on any machine. Self-limiting by design: unknown programs model as benign so it under-reports rather than inventing findings, path analysis is purely lexical (no symlink resolution), and WT03 states outright that findings UNDERSTATE exposure under bypassPermissions. Witnesses are inert - execution proved with id, every network payload targets the reserved .invalid TLD. 318 tests incl. direct reproductions of #28784 and #36637, 6 fixture policy stacks (hardened grades 100/A as the control), severity-weighted score + grade + CI exit-code gate

revenant - offline, LLM-free, dependency-free (pure-stdlib) ADOPTION-SURFACE auditor for the AGENT PERSISTENT-MEMORY plane: the store the agent writes for its own future self. The series' first entry on state the agent AUTHORS rather than state it receives - every prior entry audits an inbound or declared artifact (a static manifest 001-010, one MCP channel 011-022, the HTTP transport #023, terminal rendering #024, A2A #025-026, an MCP Apps bundle #027, the caching timeline #028, the telemetry envelope #029, header mirroring #030, a Skill's reachable closure #031, the permission policy #032) and asks 'is this artifact safe?'. revenant asks a question no content scanner asks: GIVEN that a stored memory is bad, DOES IT MATTER - will it ever be in the room, in what future session, at what authority, and what is the minimum edit that keeps it out? Motivated by a measured gap: MemSecBench (arXiv 2607.27080) reports memory poisoning PERSISTS 84.2% of the time (MPSR) but reaches end-to-end consequence only 50.3% (E2E-ASR), concluding that 'persistence is permissive; ADOPTION constitutes the decisive filtering boundary' - and every shipping defence (Ratine, OWASP Agent Memory Guard, NVIDIA SkillSpector, Cisco Watchdog) scores the WRITE. That 34-point adoption gap is unmeasured, and OWASP ASI06 (Memory and Context Poisoning, 2026 Agentic AI Top 10) names TEMPORAL DECOUPLING as the distinguishing property - exactly what a content classifier cannot see and a reachability model can. Three ideas carry it: (1) a RECALL TIER LATTICE ordered by adoption probability rather than severity - ambient (text in the always-loaded index, no gate at all) > indexed (advertised every session) > PROMOTED (not advertised but transitively reachable by [[wikilink]] from something that is, so a hidden memory rides into context behind a legitimate one - the amplification tier, and a property of the GRAPH BETWEEN items that is invisible to every per-item scanner) > gated > orphan, with the exact promotion path reported as the witness; (2) BOUNDED rather than FAKED retrieval - real recall is an embedding or an LLM judgement and neither is reproducible offline, so instead of a dishonest point estimate it computes a BAND (strict lexical = likely recalled, permissive = could be) and grades on the permissive bound because that is the one an attacker picks, with a deliberately bland description matching every probe since vagueness is how a poisoned item stays plausible to a reviewer while staying retrievable; (3) an EXACT MINIMUM-EDIT quarantine plan - severing hazards from ambient reach is a minimum edge cut over index pointers and wikilinks, solved with Edmonds-Karp max-flow rather than a greedy pass, because memory stores are hand-curated and a plan demanding eleven deletions when two suffice gets ignored and the store stays poisoned (the fixture: 4 hazards, 2 edits). 13 rules, EVERY ONE a JOINT content-AND-reach condition so content alone never yields a high severity and reach alone never yields a finding: REV001 binding directive in the always-loaded index, REV002 link promotion, REV003 undeclared payload (description shares no topic vocabulary with the directive - unannounced at BOTH the retrieval and the human review boundary, since the description is simultaneously the retrieval key and the only thing an index reader sees), REV004 scope inflation, REV005 AUTHORITY LAUNDERING (type: user/feedback asserts 'the operator told me this' - the highest trust the format can express - while the body carries third-party origin markers, so a web page is re-read as an operator instruction; motivated by arXiv 2606.24322 on origin-bound authority), REV006 descriptive type carrying a binding directive, REV007 DORMANT TRIGGER (directive deferred to 'when deploying' / 'when handling payments' - timed to the moment oversight is thinnest; arXiv 2605.28201 plant-persist-trigger), REV008 exfil sink, REV009 credential at rest, REV010 destructive directive, REV011 policy override, REV012 DANGLING PROMOTION (a link to a memory that does not exist yet is a RESERVED SEAT - whatever is written under that name later inherits ambient reach with nobody re-reviewing the linking text), REV013 orphan. Severity is ADOPTION-WEIGHTED: the identical webhook-exfiltration directive scores 80.0/critical when indexed and 10.0/low when unreachable, where a content scanner returns the same verdict for both. Honest about its own seams: structural reach (tiers, promotion paths, dangling links, the min-cut) is EXACT graph fact, while force/payload/gated-vs-orphan are heuristics; the quarantine plan states outright that cutting structure does NOT make an item unretrievable and lists what stays reachable; and it does not compete with the content scanners it names - it is the complement, deliberately shallow on payload lexicons. Two adapters (index-plus-notes markdown, flat JSON/vector export), sentence-segmented directive classification so a paragraph-in-one-string vector record does not hide its instruction after the first full stop, pointer-line suppression so a well-formed index titled 'Deploy runbook' is not read as the imperative 'deploy', and a lexicon confined to ONE reviewable file so every claim traces to a listed phrase. 141 tests, clean + poisoned reference stores with 21 documented (rule, item) ground-truth pairs asserted in BOTH directions (a new false positive fails as loudly as a missed detection), the clean store deliberately containing a legitimately BINDING memory that must stay silent; exposure score + grade + CI exit-code gate

satrap - offline, LLM-free, dependency-free (pure-stdlib) static auditor for the AGENT DELEGATION PLANE: who may spawn whom, holding what authority, and what comes back. The series' first entry on structure INSIDE the agent system - every prior entry audits an artifact at the perimeter (a static manifest 001-010, one MCP channel 011-022, the HTTP transport #023, terminal rendering #024, A2A #025-026, an MCP Apps bundle #027, the caching timeline #028, the telemetry envelope #029, header mirroring #030, a Skill's reachable file closure #031, the permission policy #032, the memory store #033) - whereas delegation is the one plane where the agent is both author and audience: it writes a task for another agent and then reads back whatever that agent says. Models authority as a point on a TWO-AXIS LATTICE (capability set x consent posture) under the product order, which makes visible the escalation a tool-list subset check cannot see: a child with strictly fewer tools at a wider posture is strictly more authorised. Resolves scope precedence (managed > cli > nearest project > user > plugin), then runs a COMBINED edge/authority least fixpoint over the delegation graph - combined because which agents a node can spawn depends on whether it inherited a delegation tool, and what it inherited depends on the path - proving that `transfer` is NOT decreasing (an omitted tools list copies the delegator's whole capability set downward, and plugin-scope definitions have their declared permissionMode silently dropped). Second plane is the RETURN CHANNEL: a subagent's report is free text spliced into the delegator's context, so untrusted content that entered tagged as data leaves wearing the child's authority - satrap enumerates ingest->raw-return->effector laundering paths and emits a greedy attribution plan to break them. 25 finding codes in 5 families (AU authority / TP topology / SC scope resolution / FL flow / DC declaration), scored 0-100 with letter grade, text+JSON+Mermaid output and a CI exit-code gate. Every AU/FL finding ships a WITNESS - a concrete delegation path replayed from the root principal through independent code before the finding is emitted, so the authority ENVELOPE (the join over all paths) is never itself evidence; unreplayable claims are suppressed and counted. Ships a sound reference corpus that scores 100/A with zero findings, a vulnerable corpus with one documented ground-truth defect per agent, and a deepchain corpus isolating topology; 127 tests, plus a verifier that walks sys.modules to prove nothing outside the standard library was ever imported

deadlatch - offline, LLM-free, dependency-free (pure-stdlib) static auditor for the AGENT HOOK PLANE: the shell commands wired to fixed points in the tool-call lifecycle, which the industry has converged on as THE deterministic runtime enforcement layer around a probabilistic agent (Claude Code hooks, Google ADK before_tool_callback, Microsoft Copilot runtime enforcement roadmapped Q1-Q2 2026). Distinct from #032 warrant in the way a compiled binary is distinct from a config file: warrant audits the DECLARATIVE allow/ask/deny rules the runtime evaluates, while hooks are ARBITRARY CODE with an exit-status contract, a decision protocol, a parallel execution model and the ability to rewrite tool input before it runs - none of warrant's failure modes exist here and none of these 49 rules could be expressed there. The thesis is that the hook contract is full of places where a refusal is ACCEPTED, LOGGED AND THEN IGNORED, and that the shared failure mode is invisible to testing: the hook still runs, still prints its refusal, and still passes every manual check its author performs, because the author verifies that the MESSAGE APPEARS, not that the CALL STOPPED. Grounded in a clean convergence of primary and secondary sources - the published reference defines the silent-failure modes (exit 2 blocks on 14 of 31 events and is DISCARDED on the other 17; permissionDecision is honoured on 4 events only; 9 events accept no matcher; 10 have closed matcher domains; matched handlers run IN PARALLEL; a timed-out handler 'does not block, normal permission flow applies') while practitioners independently report falling into exactly those modes ('the most common hook mistake is writing a security gate with exit 1 instead of exit 2 - it appears to work during testing because the warning message prints'; 'an endpoint that goes down fails open, which is the wrong default for a guardrail'), and the same layer is an EXPLOITED attack surface (CVE-2025-59536 pre-trust hook execution CVSS 8.7, CVE-2026-21852 ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL key exfiltration, the April 2026 SessionStart-hook worm, claude-code#34692 subagent hook bypass). 49 rules in 10 families: SURF (the hook never loads - unparseable settings file, missing or non-executable script, unknown event name), GATE (the flagship - denial path exiting 1 instead of 2 = CRITICAL, exit 2 on an event that discards it, permissionDecision emitted at the JSON top level instead of inside hookSpecificOutput, a gate without errexit that crashes to exit 0, escalate-only enforcement that is void under bypassPermissions), MATCH (faithful reproduction of the runtime's THREE-WAY classification decided by CHARACTERS rather than by any declared type - wildcard / exact-list / unanchored regex - so 'mcp__memory__*' is caught as a regex in which * quantifies the preceding UNDERSCORE, with 'Write*' flagged and '.*Edit' deliberately not), COVER (capability-equivalence classes make 'you gated Write but not Edit or NotebookEdit' a mechanical result rather than an opinion; plus no mcp__ branch, ungated delegation, disableAllHooks, and gates that live only in a gitignored file), INJECT (${tool_input.command} interpolated into a shell string the model then controls), EXFIL (transcript piped off-box, credential-shaped env vars in an http handler, ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL rewritten), TRUST (pre-trust event in a committed settings file, curl|bash, verdict delegated to an MCP server), RACE, BUDGET, IF. Same observation/judgement split as #023 rampart: discover.py is the ONLY module that opens a file and analyzer.py is pure (no I/O, no clock, no randomness), so a live scan and a committed capture grade through IDENTICAL code and a surface can be re-audited in CI months later - and test_architecture.py enforces the boundary MECHANICALLY by walking each module's AST and failing if a judgement module imports os/pathlib/time/random/socket/subprocess. Every finding carries CERTAIN (decidable from the declared configuration and the frozen spec tables, true by construction) or LIKELY (additionally rests on a textual reading of shell, always quoting its evidence line) - and the honesty of that split earned its keep during the build, when a naive left-to-right quote counter reported "$(printf '%s' "$payload")" as unquoted and produced four false positives in the HARDENED example; command substitution restarts the quoting context, the scanner now tracks substitution depth with a stack, and a test pins it. Deliberately NOT a dynamic prober (which would have to execute the very curl|bash it exists to warn about - rejected on the merits, not on effort). Ships two worked surfaces: examples/vulnerable trips 46 of the 49 rules and examples/hardened is the same policy configured so the gate holds (clean above LOW), both under agent-config/ rather than .claude/ so no agent can load them as real policy and every host under the reserved .invalid TLD so the demo is inert by construction - with tests that fail the build if either stops being true. scan/capture/audit/rules CLI, text+JSON+SARIF output, 137 tests green under both unittest and pytest, zero runtime dependencies.

sluice - offline, LLM-free, dependency-free (pure-stdlib) static auditor for the AGENT NETWORK-EGRESS PLANE: the allow/deny domain lists that decide where an agent's bytes may go. The series' first entry on the NETWORK layer - every prior entry audits a static manifest (001-010), one MCP channel (011-022), a transport or rendering surface (023-024), an A2A artifact (025-026), a client-side or protocol plane (027-031), or structure inside the agent system: the permission policy it consults (#032 warrant), the memory it writes (#033 revenant), who it may spawn (#034 satrap), the hooks wired to its tool calls (#035 deadlatch). sluice asks the one question none of those ask: not which tool may run, but where the bytes may go. The thesis is that an egress allowlist is the LAST MECHANICAL control between a prompt-injected agent and the internet - every other defence in the stack is probabilistic - and that it is universally graded on 'does the build still work?' rather than on 'does every entry TERMINATE an exfiltration?'. Usually not, and structurally rather than carelessly: *.amazonaws.com is every S3 bucket on Earth, github.com is every gist, docs.google.com is a Forms prefilled-submission URL that turns a GET into a write into someone else's spreadsheet, cdn.jsdelivr.net is all of npm and all of GitHub behind one hostname, and dns.google is a channel the allowlist cannot even see because a destination list constrains the host you connect to and never the name you ask about. Each passes every test its author runs, because the author verifies that THE DEPENDENCY STILL DOWNLOADS, not that THE CHANNEL IS CLOSED. The flagship rule family is derived from published data rather than from opinion: the Public Suffix List's PRIVATE section is, read sideways, a REGISTRY OF NAMESPACES WHOSE LEAVES ARE RENTED (s3.amazonaws.com, workers.dev, github.io, blob.core.windows.net all exist in it to record that names below that point are handed to third parties), so a wildcard egress entry written at a public-suffix boundary is MECHANICALLY a grant of a namespace an attacker can obtain a name in - which makes *.amazonaws.com and *.com the SAME FINDING at different severities instead of two hand-maintained special cases, with the curated corpus supplying only what the PSL cannot (how cheaply a leaf is obtained, and the cases where tenancy is a URL path rather than a DNS label, since a gist has no subdomain). 57 rules in 12 families: TENANCY (the flagship - exact-boundary grants split anonymous/CRITICAL vs purchasable/HIGH, plus TEN006 for wildcards NESTED above rented namespaces, the *.amazonaws.com case the exact-boundary rules miss because amazonaws.com is not itself a suffix while six of its children are), WRITABLE (forges, package registries, paste and file-drop hosts), CHANNEL (collectors, chat webhooks - api.telegram.org takes the payload in a GET query string so exfiltration needs no body and no POST - form sinks, mail relays), MIRROR (CDNs that re-serve whole ecosystems, and general fetch proxies that restore the entire internet through one approved hostname), REDIRECT, RESOLVER (DoH endpoints, and the fact that refused connections are still RESOLVED), INTERNAL (the side of the boundary nobody writes rules for: instance metadata, loopback, the in-cluster API server), PRECEDENCE, FAILMODE (the control configured and not in force - prompting instead of refusing, which is a control only while a human is attached), COVER, SHAPE, REACH. Five host profiles modelled from vendor documentation and public disclosure (reference / claude-code / vscode / copilot-cloud / naive-proxy, the last modelling the in-house plain-suffix-test shape a 2026 disclosure showed admitting attacker-host\x00.allowed.com when the string test and the C resolver disagreed about where the hostname ended), so `sluice diff` demonstrates ONE configuration confining DIFFERENTLY depending on which runtime loads it - identical bytes, different outcome, nobody having edited a line. Same observation/judgement split as #023 rampart and #035 deadlatch: discover.py is the ONLY module that opens a file, every judgement module is pure, and test_architecture.py walks each module's AST and fails the build if a judgement module imports os/pathlib/time/random/socket/subprocess - which ALSO enforces the invariant that sluice NEVER OPENS A CONNECTION, because auditing an egress policy by testing reachability means making exactly the requests the policy exists to prevent from exactly the machine it exists to confine (a dynamic prober was rejected on the merits, not on effort: it is indistinguishable from the attack to every monitor watching, and failing to reach a sink proves nothing about that sink next Tuesday). CERTAIN vs LIKELY split earned its keep twice - the embedded PSL is a curated subset so unrecognised names fall back to the implicit rule and are reported as LIKELY with the name's SHAPE quoted as evidence, and every finding resting on modelled runtime behaviour rather than on the declared file is LIKELY by construction with `sluice hosts` printing each profile's provenance so a reader can check the model rather than trust it. Two design corrections during the build are visible in the rules: the reach metric originally counted PROMPTS as admissions and scored every policy on a prompting runtime at 99%, burying the entries that genuinely widen it (prompts are now reported separately - except for destinations INSIDE the boundary, where 'it asks first' is not a denial); and SHAPE008 originally graded a denied metadata IP as HIGH, penalising the exact hardening INT001 asks for, so address-level denials are now LOW and worded as necessary-but-not-sufficient. Ships two worked surfaces in sluice's vendor-neutral format rather than at any runtime's real settings path - with a test that fails the build if a .claude/, .vscode/ or copilot-firewall.json path ever appears in the tree, since an auditor whose fixtures are themselves a working permissive config would be an unusually embarrassing way to introduce the problem it detects: examples/porous is a policy a careful engineer would ship and a reviewer would approve (39 findings across all 12 families, nothing in it careless), examples/tight is the same workload closed - not shorter, DIFFERENT - with zero CRITICAL, zero HIGH, nothing CERTAIN above LOW, and identical confinement under every profile. scan/capture/audit/simulate/diff/explain/rules/hosts CLI, text+JSON+SARIF output, 260-destination offline probe corpus, 218 tests green under both pytest and unittest, zero runtime dependencies.

entrepot - offline, LLM-free, dependency-free (pure-stdlib) EMERGENT-RISK auditor for the MCP AGGREGATION/FEDERATION PLANE: the first entry whose unit of analysis is the composition rather than a component. Replays the merge bottom-up and reports what the aggregation boundary destroyed (shadowed names, laundered annotations, erased provenance, flattened identity) plus the lethal trifecta assembled across upstreams none of which carries all three legs alone

reprise - offline, LLM-free, dependency-free (pure-stdlib) RE-EXECUTION SAFETY MODEL CHECKER for agent tool stacks: the series first entry on the RETRY / RE-DISPATCH plane. Given a declarative retry profile (tool manifest + nested retry layers + idempotency key derivation + Tasks retention TTL) it proves, per (tool x fault class), how many times an external side effect can actually COMMIT - splitting faults into DEFINITIVE (never dispatched, retry is free) vs AMBIGUOUS (dispatched, outcome unknown, retry duplicates), multiplying nested attempt budgets, and evaluating idempotency-key survival PER LAYER BOUNDARY (a content key stops a transport replay but not an agent replan that re-derives args). Grades key sources STABLE/VOLATILE/BUCKETED/SUSPECT to catch dedup schemes that are inert at runtime, flags key collisions that silently drop a real call, models the MCP MRTR input_required re-send as a pseudo-layer no retry budget caps, and catches retry budgets that outlive Tasks result retention. 14 rules, counterexample schedule per finding, CI gate.

halflife - offline, LLM-free, dependency-free (pure-stdlib) RESIDENCY MODEL CHECKER for the AGENT CONTEXT-COMPACTION plane: the series' first entry whose subject is not an artifact but the WINDOW OF TIME an artifact is in force. Every prior entry audits something PRESENT - a static manifest (001-010), one MCP channel (011-022), the HTTP transport (#023), terminal rendering (#024), A2A (#025-026), an MCP Apps bundle (#027), the caching timeline (#028), the telemetry envelope (#029), header mirroring (#030), a Skill's reachable closure (#031), the permission policy (#032), the memory store (#033), the delegation graph (#034), the hook plane (#035), the egress list (#036), a federation merge (#037), a retry profile (#038) - and every one of them silently assumes the artifact is STILL IN THE ROOM when it matters. halflife audits that assumption. A governance constraint binds an agent only while it is RESIDENT in the context window; a compaction policy is a schedule for removing things from that window; therefore the operative question is not 'is this policy well written' but 'is it still there at turn 47, which compaction event took it, and what fired afterwards'. Grounded in a measured number rather than an intuition: ConstraintRot (arXiv 2606.22528, 1,323 episodes x 7 model families) reports policy violation at 0% with the policy in full context, 30% pooled after compaction (59% worst model), and - the decisive split - 0% when the constraint SURVIVES the summary against 38% when it is DROPPED, concluding that survival, not content, is the filtering boundary. Survival is not semantic, it is SCHEDULING, and a declared token profile plus a declared compaction policy makes it exactly decidable offline with no model call. Three ideas carry it: (1) SEVERITY INVERTED BY FORCE - the same paper measures soft organisational policy decaying +50 points under compaction against +6 for hard safety norms, an 8.3x gap, because a model re-derives 'do not exfiltrate an SSH key' from its weights with the policy absent and re-derives NOTHING about 'vendor email goes through legal' or 'deploy only to eu-west-1', so halflife grades an evicted SOFT constraint CRITICAL and an evicted HARD one HIGH - the opposite of every severity-by-topic scanner, and the correct ordering for this plane; (2) TRIGGER STEERING (HL-EVICT003), the observation that compaction fires on a TOKEN THRESHOLD, so whoever controls the SIZE of what the agent ingests controls WHEN it fires, and residency is a function of that phase - a constraint comfortably resident at a call today is made non-resident by PADDING an earlier untrusted turn, with no instruction injected and no content filter tripped, the fetched page merely bigger; every witness is found by ladder search and then RE-SIMULATED before emission, so an unproven steering claim is never reported (the shipped example: pad turn 8 by 31,331 tokens, one new compaction event lands between the policy and the call, C-004 goes RESIDENT -> SUMMARIZER_DEPENDENT at the spend.commit on turn 16); (3) A REPAIR THAT REPLAYS ITSELF - the paper's defence is constraint pinning (0% violation restored across all seven models at ~47 tokens), real harnesses give a BOUNDED pinning region, so 'which constraints do I pin' is an exact 0/1 knapsack solved by DP rather than greedily (a plan demanding eleven pins when three suffice gets ignored and the session stays ungoverned) - but pinned tokens are RESIDENT FROM TURN ZERO and push the window toward the trigger sooner, so a pin plan can OPEN a gap for a constraint it did not select, which the '<0.5% overhead' framing hides and which halflife reports by re-simulating the plan it just computed. Residency is a THREE-state lattice and the third state is an admission: RESIDENT, EVICTED (structurally deleted - CERTAIN), and SUMMARIZER_DEPENDENT (handed to a model-authored summary, whose contents halflife REFUSES to predict, grading on the pessimistic bound because that is the bound an adversary selects for and because 0% and 38% are not close enough to average) - with TRANSCODING DEPTH, the exact count of summarisation passes traversed, reported alongside, since at depth >=2 the window holds a paraphrase of a paraphrase that no author reviewed. 24 rules in 6 families: RES (the flagship governance gap, evicted vs summariser-dependent, transcoding depth, never-resident ordering defects, orphan constraints, ungoverned effectors), CHAN (placement - the constraint written in a channel this harness compacts while it preserves another, untrusted-origin policy, a policy whose only carrier is a tool result under a tier that clears tool results on a schedule, split governance where half a policy outlives the rest and reads as the whole), EVICT (the Compaction-Eviction Attack shape from the same paper - summariser-directed text co-resident with a constraint the same event hands to the same summariser - plus supersession claims and trigger steering), LAUNDER (the summarisation boundary destroys channel labels, so content that entered tagged as data leaves as narration in the trusted prefix; and the tier race where the cheap tier DELETES a tool result after the expensive tier already absorbed it, leaving a conclusion whose source cannot be re-checked), CFG (the shipped `instructions` parameter COMPLETELY REPLACES the default summarisation prompt rather than extending it, so a string naming three things to keep is also a string that stopped asking for everything else; pause_after_compaction configured with no inspection step; triggers outside documented bounds; a policy that cannot reduce the window), PIN. Seven harness profiles each carrying a citable provenance string printed by `halflife profiles` - api-compaction and api-compaction-tuned (Messages API compact_20260112, trigger 150000, minimum 50000, the tuned variant configured exactly as the documentation's own examples configure it), coding-agent (the three tiers: microcompact clearing stale tool results with NO model call, full compact, session-memory compact), sliding-window (the honest worst case, where eviction is CERTAIN rather than summariser-dependent), structured-eviction (CWL, arXiv 2606.11213), event-log (Scroll, arXiv 2608.21690, modelling recoverable eviction - and halflife still reports the gap, because recoverability is not residency and a constraint the agent must CHOOSE to look up does not bind the choice), pinned - which makes the headline demo a DIFFERENTIAL: one session, seven compaction policies, seven different governance outcomes, nobody having edited a line. Ships two worked sessions with IDENTICAL token profiles, turn counts, channels and call sequences, differing only in WHERE each constraint was written: examples/decaying is a session a careful engineer ships and a reviewer approves (31 findings under api-compaction, nothing in it careless) and examples/durable is the same workload placed well - not shorter, PLACED DIFFERENTLY - which grades 100/A with ZERO findings on the two profiles that re-inject the channels it used and fails on the rest, because policy placement is only durable RELATIVE TO A HARNESS. Two results fell out that the design did not anticipate: the LLM-free tool-result-clearing tier PRESERVES governance markedly better than summarisation does, because the thing eating the window is tool output rather than policy; and durable under the event-log profile has zero findings under replay yet five CRITICALs from trigger steering alone - clean only for as long as nobody chooses the size of what the agent reads. Same observation/judgement split as #023 rampart, #035 deadlatch and #036 sluice: loader.py is the ONLY module that opens a file, every judgement module is a pure transform, and test_architecture.py walks each module's AST and fails the build if a judgement module imports os/pathlib/time/random/socket/subprocess or calls open() - the same walk enforcing the harder invariant that NOTHING in the package imports a network module or a model SDK, since auditing governance decay by shipping the pre-compaction transcript to a model would be a strange way to protect a session; and the guard is itself tested against synthetic bad source, because a guard that cannot fail is decoration. A live transcript instrumenter was rejected ON THE MERITS, not on effort: it answers 'did THIS summary drop the policy' (one sample of a stochastic process) rather than 'does this CONFIGURATION hand the policy to a summariser at all' (a property of the system), it cannot be re-derived in CI six months later, and it requires the transcript to leave the machine. Two design corrections are visible in the rules: HL-CFG004 originally fired on the mere PRESENCE of a hard constraint, penalising a session that had correctly written it into a preserved channel and recommending a pinning region to an author who no longer needed one, and now fires only for hard constraints that actually degrade; and the pin mechanism was silently defeated by re-assertion, selecting five constraints, spending 167 tokens and closing ZERO witnesses while reporting a plan - caught only because the planner verifies by replay instead of trusting itself, which is the entire argument for building it that way. scan via audit/simulate/diff/pin/explain/rules/profiles CLI, text+JSON+SARIF output, severity-weighted score + letter grade + CI exit-code gate, lexicon confined to ONE reviewable file of 36 phrases with every textual finding quoting its match in context, 217 tests green under both pytest and unittest, zero runtime dependencies.

sleight - offline, LLM-free, dependency-free (pure-stdlib) PATH DENOTATION AUDITOR for the AGENT WORKSPACE-CONFINEMENT plane: the roots and deny globs that decide which files an agent may touch. The series' first entry whose unit of analysis is the FILESYSTEM NAMING FUNCTION itself. Every prior entry audits a static manifest (001-010), one MCP channel (011-022), a transport or rendering surface (023-024), an A2A artifact (025-026), a client-side or protocol plane (027-031), or structure inside the agent system - the permission policy it consults (#032 warrant), the memory it writes (#033 revenant), who it may spawn (#034 satrap), its hooks (#035 deadlatch), where its bytes may go (#036 sluice), how its servers compose (#037 entrepot), what happens on retry (#038 reprise), what survives compaction (#039 halflife) - and every one of them SHARES ONE ASSUMPTION: that a path is a name for one object. sleight attacks that assumption. The thesis: a confinement policy is a predicate over path STRINGS while the filesystem is a MANY-TO-ONE, UNSTABLE NAMING FUNCTION, so the policy is sound only where each string names exactly one object and keeps naming it - which on a real developer's machine is almost nowhere. The formal frame is three functions that are supposed to agree about which object is in play: judge(n) the verdict the policy engine returns, show(n) the string put in front of the human for approval, open(n) the object the kernel reaches. EVERY 2026 DISCLOSURE IN THIS SPACE IS TWO OF THOSE THREE DISAGREEING, which is why one 50-rule catalog covers a symlink, an inode, a Unicode normalization form and a .git file that is not a directory: GhostApproval (CWE-61 + CWE-451, six assistants - Amazon Q, Claude Code, Augment, Cursor, Antigravity, Windsurf) is show != open, the approval dialog showing a repo filename while the write lands in ~/.ssh/authorized_keys; CVE-2026-32232 (ZeptoClaw) names dangling-symlink, TOCTOU and HARDLINK bypass in one advisory; the OpenClaw assertSandboxPath race and rsync CVE-2026-29518 are judge and open evaluated at different instants against a mutable tree; Cursor's git-metadata finding is judge matching a directory component that a 'gitdir:' pointer has moved; MagicDot, 8.3 aliases and Win32 trailing-dot stripping are the VOLUME folding two spellings together after the string comparison already happened. 50 rules in 9 families named for the MECHANISM that drove the three apart - LINK, ALIAS, INDIRECT, DISPLAY, TIMING, BOUNDARY, DENY, WRITE, SHAPE. The centrepiece is a RESOLUTION AUTOMATON that keeps the DERIVATION realpath() throws away, classifying every aliasing step as either a cuttable EDGE (symlink/junction/gitfile: an object you can delete) or an uncuttable FOLD (case/NFC-NFD/8.3/stream/trailing-dot: a property of the volume) - so `sleight cut` computes an exact MINIMUM HITTING SET over the escape witnesses (4 objects closing 5 escapes on the porous fixture, one fewer than naive because a two-hop chain and a direct link share a hop) AND, more usefully, reports the 9 escapes NO CUT CAN CLOSE, naming the real remedy instead of proposing one that would not work: 'hardlink: the object has two directory entries of equal standing and deleting either leaves the other; fix by comparing device+inode after open'. A TOOL THAT IDENTIFIES WHEN ITS OWN CLASS OF REMEDIATION IS INAPPLICABLE. Constructive-witness discipline carried forward from #032: sleight never says 'case-insensitivity is dangerous', it SYNTHESIZES the exact other spelling (.ENV, .env., .env::$DATA, SECRET~1.JSO, secrets.json:backup), re-resolves it, and emits it only if it lands on the object, so every finding carries a name you can paste into a shell - enforced by tests asserting every emitted spelling round-trips and every escape witness in the shipped fixture reaches the referent the report names. 5 modelled runtimes x 3 modelled volumes make `sleight diff` show ONE tree and ONE policy confining DIFFERENTLY depending on who opens it (reference lets 1 object out, lexical lets 5 out with 24 criticals against 5 - and this is not hypothetical: GhostApproval was fixed in THREE OF SIX products, so handing the same repo to two agents genuinely produces two outcomes today). The `reference` profile - the runtime you would build if you took the 2026 disclosures as requirements - exists to give the report a floor, and produces the result the tool exists to be able to state: A CORRECTLY BUILT CHECKER STILL DOES NOT CONFINE THE WORKSPACE, because the one remaining escape is a hardlink, a property of the tree rather than of the checker. Severity is derived, not declared: fixtures never label themselves, the REFERENT is matched against a corpus carrying SEPARATE read_class and write_class (authorized_keys is near-worthless to read and remote code execution to write - exactly why the GhostApproval chain targeted a write, and why a read-only confinement model would have called that repo clean). Same observation/judgement split as #023/#035/#036: capture.py is the ONLY module that touches a filesystem, test_architecture.py walks every other module's AST and fails the build on os/pathlib/io/socket/subprocess/time/random - which ALSO enforces that sleight NEVER TESTS AN ESCAPE BY ATTEMPTING ONE (a dynamic prober was rejected on the merits: verifying the reach means performing the read the audit exists to prove is possible, from the machine where it matters, and it is false comfort anyway since a link that dangles today resolves the moment someone creates the target). Two design corrections are visible in the rules: DISPLAY findings originally graded every divergence at base severity and rated an ordinary monorepo symlink CRITICAL, so in-boundary divergences now cap at MEDIUM; and SHP002 originally fired on every well-written allow rule because 'dir/**' and 'dir/*' disagree about whether they match 'dir' itself, so it now reports only the direction that ADMITS MORE. Test_catalog reads analyze.py's AST and fails if the catalog documents a rule no pass can emit - it caught LNK002 documented-and-unreachable during the build. Two worked surfaces on the SAME NTFS volume (the remedy is the policy, not a friendlier filesystem): examples/plausible is a repo a reviewer would approve - monorepo symlink, git worktree layout, a build cache made with ln instead of cp, a shared docs junction, a group-writable CI directory - producing 63 findings across all nine families and 14 escape witnesses; examples/confined is the same workload closed, zero escapes under every runtime, grade A, monorepo link still working. The single change that did it is the finding the experiment did not expect to produce: ON A FOLDING VOLUME A DENY LIST CANNOT BE CLOSED AND AN ALLOW LIST CAN, because closing a deny list requires the matcher to fold exactly as the volume folds on all four axes forever, while an unrecognised spelling simply matches no allow rule. capture/scan/audit/diff/cut/explain/rules/profiles CLI, text+JSON+SARIF, CI exit-code gate, 380 tests green under both pytest and unittest, zero runtime dependencies.

parallax - offline, LLM-free, dependency-free (pure-stdlib) PROJECTION AUDITOR for the MCP TOOL-RESULT plane: the series' first entry on the RETURN LEG of a tool call. A tools/call result is not one message, it is a broadcast to two readers with different parsers - the human who approves the action and the model that acts on it - and MCP 2026-07-28 gives a server three ways to hand them different things: annotations.audience addresses one reader by design, the content/structuredContent equivalence is a SHOULD nothing enforces, and every client decides for itself what it renders and what it drops. parallax computes BOTH projections under six client behaviour profiles and reports every divergence: amount and destination differing between the prose and the payload, a model-only block speaking in the imperative, a human who reads 'completed successfully' while the model reads 'rollback failed', an embedded resource on a host the displayed link never mentions, and a chat client's three-block render cap doing the same hiding with no annotation involved at all. Three design corrections are visible in the code, all caught by tests: PX-501/502 originally compared raw projected text, which made the spec's OWN advice to mirror structuredContent into a TextContent block fire on every conforming result including the benign baseline, and now compare canonical fact sets; the structured-first profile originally starved the model on any result with no structuredContent, which no shipping client does; and PX-105 handed the magnitude case to PX-106 on the field NAME while PX-106 fired on the RATIO, so a sub-magnitude divergence on a field called amount fell through both and was reported by neither. 48 rules across five families (mirror/audience/errors/channel/cross) via audit/project/diff/remediate/rules/explain/profiles/demo CLI, text+JSON+SARIF output, severity-weighted score + letter grade + CI exit-code gate, ordered remediation plan, bundled JSON Schema subset validator that reports unsupported keywords rather than silently passing them, lexicon confined to ONE reviewable file of 68 phrases with every textual finding quoting its match in context, 353 tests green under both pytest and unittest, zero runtime dependencies, never executes a tool or resolves a URI it reads

undertow - offline, LLM-free, dependency-free (pure-stdlib) RESIDUE & DUPLICATION AUDITOR for the MCP CANCELLATION / ABORT plane: the series' first entry on the STOP leg. Experiments 001-041 all audit an agent going FORWARD - what it may call, read, remember, spawn, retry or return. undertow audits what happens when someone pulls the plug. The thesis is a contradiction inside a single spec revision: MCP 2026-07-28 made cancellation IMPLICIT on Streamable HTTP ('closing the SSE response stream is the cancellation signal; the server MUST treat a client disconnect as cancellation') in the same release that REMOVED stream resumability (SEP-2575: 'a broken response stream loses the in-flight request; clients MUST re-issue it as a new request with a new request ID'). Those are ONE network event with TWO mandated readings - 'stop' to the server, 'run it again under a fresh identity' to the client - with nothing synchronising them and no bound on stop latency, which also means requestId-keyed server-side deduplication is PROVABLY unable to match the retry the spec itself requires. Given a captured JSON-RPC session (JSONL, both transports) plus an effect profile declaring when each tool's side effects become DURABLE, undertow computes the RESIDUE WINDOW [cancel_ts, last observed server activity] of every cancelled request and classifies each declared effect as COMMITTED (durable before the cancel arrived) / RACING (landed inside the window - the cancel lost) / AVOIDED, flagging any external uncompensated effect in the first two as UNRECOVERABLE; and fingerprints requests (canonical JSON minus _meta and declared volatile args) to pair a cancelled request with its re-issue and decide whether a STABLE IDEMPOTENCY KEY survived the transition (suppressed) or the work provably ran twice under two different request IDs (confirmed double dispatch). 26 rules in 6 families - cancel-channel conformance (late response, unreleased slot per codex #20925, cancel of unknown/completed requests, the new 2026-07-28 MUST NOT on server-sent notifications/cancelled outside subscriptions/listen, disconnect not honoured, post-cancel emission, orphan/late progress tokens), liveness (progress-keepalive timeout defeat via the spec's own MAY-reset-the-clock clause, missing timeout ceiling, excessive stop latency), the duplication channel, task lifecycle (a task handle outliving the cancellation that should have stopped it; cooperative tasks/cancel never confirmed terminal), effect residue and capture coverage - with severity-weighted scoring, per-rule deduction caps, categorical grade clamps and a CI exit-code gate. Ships four ground-truth fixtures whose exact rule sets are asserted by tests: conformant-stdio (zero findings, 100/A), conformant-http (one INFO - duplication suppressed by a stable key, 100/A), defective-stdio (10 rules, 47/F) and defective-http (23 rules, 2 critical / 9 high / 14 medium, 0/F) built around a money-moving flagship where a stop is ignored for 1200ms, the debit commits INSIDE the residue window uncompensated, and the client re-issues the identical transfer 800ms later under a new request ID. 5137 LOC, 211 tests, zero runtime dependencies

skein - offline, LLM-free, dependency-free (pure-stdlib) SERIALIZABILITY & INTERFERENCE AUDITOR for the AGENT PARALLEL TOOL-CALL plane: the series' first entry on the INTERLEAVING leg. Experiments 001-042 all audit calls ONE AT A TIME - what a call may do (001-010), what one channel promises (011-021), what the seams between channels leak (022), what happens on retry (038), on cancel (042), on the way back (041) - and every one of them assumes the calls happened IN SOME ORDER. skein audits the case where they did not. The thesis is a collision between two 2026 releases: MCP 2026-07-28 deleted protocol sessions and told servers that need cross-call state to mint an explicit handle and have the model PASS IT BACK AS AN ORDINARY TOOL ARGUMENT (SEP-2567), while both major labs shipped wide parallel-subagent modes and orchestration harnesses that batch every tool call a model emits in one turn. Together those rebuild the oldest bug in databases out of parts nobody thinks of as a database: shared mutable state addressed by a value the MODEL holds, mutated by calls dispatched with no ordering between them, against effects that sometimes cannot be undone. The 2026 literature saw it and answered with RUNTIMES - Atomix's transactional settlement (arXiv 2602.14849), CoAgent's monotonic pre-order (arXiv 2606.15376), three verified Rust runtimes realising an L0-L4 consistency hierarchy (arXiv 2606.17182) - each correct, each asking you to replace your execution layer, and none able to say anything about the sessions you already logged. skein is the cheap half nobody shipped. Given a captured session (JSONL, with actor identity so a main agent and its subagents are ONE capture, and batch identity so the model's issue order is recoverable) plus a declarative effect profile saying what each tool reads / writes / appends / deletes / enumerates, it builds the CONFLICT GRAPH of the observed schedule - a provably-ordered conflict contributes one directed edge, a CONCURRENT conflict contributes both, because the capture does not say which way it went - and a strongly connected component is then a set of invocations for which NO SERIAL ORDER reproduces what happened. 26 rules in 6 families: serialization (non-serializable region via Tarjan SCC with a shortest-cycle witness, lost update, dirty read, write skew across a declared invariant, non-repeatable read, tool-effect reordering), staleness (a raced read whose value reaches a LATER call's arguments - the race that became a wrong ACTION, not just a wrong value; phantom enumeration; read/write and read/delete races), causality (provenance violation: a call issued carrying a value whose first appearance anywhere in the capture is the result of a call that had not finished - the model minted a handle the server was supposed to mint), irreversibility (uncompensable external effect INSIDE a conflict cycle, which is critical because the schedule has no serial equivalent AND cannot be rolled back to obtain one), isolation hygiene (exclusive violated, a parallel_safe claim contradicted by an observed conflict, cross-actor write collision - the worktree isolates the working DIRECTORY, not the ledger) and coverage, where every undecidable question becomes a finding rather than a silent skip. Also emits a SERIALIZATION PLAN: each observed batch re-partitioned into conflict-free waves by greedy colouring, so the output is a fix and not only a verdict. STA01/STA02/CAU01/CAU03/SER06 are the detection-side counterparts of the four anomalies formalised in TLA+ by arXiv:2606.17182 (stale-generation, phantom-tool, causal-cascade, tool-effect reordering). Severity-weighted scoring with per-rule deduction caps and categorical grade clamps, text + JSON, CI exit-code gate. Four ground-truth fixtures whose exact rule sets, counts, scores and grades are asserted by tests: clean-coding and clean-commerce both 0 findings / 100 / A (they exercise append/append commutativity, prefix disjointness, an exclusive tool scheduled correctly and a benign cross-actor overlap - every path a sloppy conflict matrix false-positives on), defective-coding (14 rules, 10 high / 11 medium / 1 low, 0/F: two fs.edit calls on one file in one batch, a subagent writing it from outside, a listing racing all three, a config read whose stale value reaches a later git.commit) and defective-commerce (17 rules, 2 CRITICAL / 11 high / 16 medium / 2 low, 0/F: two payments.charge and a cart.add_item in one batch form a 3-invocation region with an uncompensable ledger write inside it). 7597 LOC, 563 tests, zero runtime dependencies
